reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: Compare the numbers: 108 ___ 100. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 10 ___ 190. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 150 ___ 50. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 25 ___ 45. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 210 ___ 176. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The stems match the competency verb and symbols directly: 'Compare the numbers: 210 ___ 176. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' with key '>' at seed 46, and each of seeds 42-45 likewise requires the pupil to select a relational symbol rather than compute, which is exactly what comparing numbers demands.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency explicitly names three symbols, '=, >, and <', but no sample ever keys '='. Seeds 42, 44 and 46 key '>' and seeds 43 and 45 key '<'; equality appears only as a distractor. The equal-numbers case, which is the one pupils most often misjudge when digit counts differ in appearance, is never generated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Two-number comparisons stated in one short line are appropriate for Grade 3 Quarter 1, and pairs like 108 versus 100 (seed 42) and 210 versus 176 (seed 46) usefully require place-value reasoning rather than mere digit counting.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only the fill-in-the-symbol frame is present. Missing are ordering three or more numbers, comparing a number written in words against one in figures, and comparing numbers with different digit counts at the four-digit level. The distractor 'cannot be determined' appears in all five seeds and is never a legitimate response when two whole numbers are both given, so it wastes an option slot in every item.

competency_alignment.rationale: The seeds show no ordered build: seed 45 compares 25 with 45, a Grade 1 level pair, while the hardest item, seed 46's 210 versus 176, is still a 3-digit comparison. Difficulty never advances toward the 4-digit place-value discrimination (for example 4 508 versus 4 580) that this competency exists to develop.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency ceiling is 10 000, yet the largest number in any sample is 210 (seed 46) and three of the five seeds stay under 200. No 4-digit number appears at all, so the pool tests roughly two percent of the stated range and never exercises comparison at thousands place value.
